summary: The candidate reserves the internal client IDs `ubiquity-passport` and `auth-hub` in shared client resolution, managed-client creation, generic agent client resolution, and device-login start; it restricts `requireTokenUser` to first-party passkey/password hub claims and gates the legacy auth-hub exchange on an explicit migration marker or a pre-cutover `createdAt`, with regression coverage. No actionable defects were found.

evidence: `src/auth_config.ts` lines 46-49 define `RESERVED_CLIENT_IDS` and line 236 rejects reserved IDs before registered-client lookup in `resolveClient`.
`src/passport.ts` lines 1485-1490 reject reserved IDs in `agentClientInput`, and lines 2340-2345 reject them in `handleAgentLoginStart`.
`src/passport.ts` lines 727-740 require `auth` to be `passkey` or `password` in `requireTokenUser`, so generic SSO and agent-token claims cannot manage grants.

`src/passport.ts` lines 2235-2244 classify legacy self grants from `legacyMigration` or a pre-cutover `createdAt`, and `src/auth_store.ts` lines 1485-1502 record `legacyMigration: false` for fresh auth-hub grants; tests cover these paths.
